name: Westward
description: Honestly one of the best outdoor spots in the city. You grab an Adirondack chair right on the gravel beach and stare straight across Lake Union with a glass of wine and a plate of oysters. There's a fire pit if it gets cool, and the whole vibe is like a casual beach bonfire that just happens to have exceptional food.
comeHereFor: Lakefront Adirondack chairs and raw bar on the beach
sunDetails: South-facing across Lake Union, full afternoon and evening sun

name: Ray's Cafe
description: The deck at Ray's is the quintessential Seattle summer experience. A sprawling second-floor balcony hanging right over Shilshole Bay with an unobstructed view of Puget Sound and the Olympics. On sunny evenings, the sunsets here are genuinely legendary. Servers will bring blankets when it cools down so you don't have to leave.
comeHereFor: Legendary waterfront sunsets over the Olympics
sunDetails: West-facing over Shilshole Bay, full afternoon and sunset sun over the Olympics

name: The Nest
description: You check in downstairs and they take you up with a special key — which already sets the mood. The rooftop terrace opens up to a jaw-dropping panorama of Elliott Bay, the Great Wheel, and the Olympic Mountains. In summer the golden-hour light over the water is genuinely hard to beat. Fire pits, lush greenery, and cozy lounge seating.
comeHereFor: Unobstructed Elliott Bay sunset views above Pike Place
sunDetails: West-facing toward Elliott Bay and Olympic Mountains, spectacular afternoon and sunset

name: Little Water Cantina
description: Little Water's patio is perched right on the eastern shore of Lake Union with a sweeping west-facing view toward Gas Works Park and the Olympics. The covered, heated setup means you can catch that afternoon glow even on cooler days. Margaritas in hand with that view is a combo that's hard to argue with.
comeHereFor: Lake Union views and margaritas on a heated lakeside patio
sunDetails: West-facing over Lake Union toward Gas Works Park, afternoon and golden hour sun

name: Marination Ma Kai
description: You order at the counter, grab a picnic table right on the waterfront, and look straight across at the full Seattle skyline — Space Needle included. The Hawaiian-Korean food is casual and really good, and the vibe on a sunny day is pure summer energy with people hanging out, dogs everywhere, and ferries passing by.
comeHereFor: The best skyline view in the city from a picnic table
sunDetails: East-facing across Elliott Bay toward Seattle skyline, morning and midday sun

name: Six Seven at The Edgewater
description: This is the patio that made me want to build this site. Sitting right over Elliott Bay with the Olympic Mountains in the distance, Six Seven has one of the best sunset views in the city. The food is elevated Pacific Northwest, and the cocktails are strong.
comeHereFor: Sunset drinks right on the water
sunDetails: West-facing over Elliott Bay, full afternoon and sunset sun

name: Cove
description: Cove's courtyard patio on Capitol Hill is a cozy escape from the neighborhood buzz. It's partially covered and heated, which means it works year-round. The food is solid New American, the cocktails are well-crafted, and the space has a warmth to it that keeps you lingering.
comeHereFor: Year-round courtyard dining on Cap Hill
sunDetails: Courtyard setting, midday sun

name: White Swan Public House
description: This is the hidden gem of the list. Tucked into a marina on Eastlake, the patio at White Swan feels like you've stumbled onto someone's private dock. Sailboats bobbing around you, solid food, and a vibe that feels genuinely off the beaten path.
comeHereFor: Hidden marina patio among the sailboats
sunDetails: Hidden marina patio, afternoon sun among the boats

name: The Mountaineering Club
description: Riding the elevator up to the 16th floor of the Graduate Hotel and stepping out onto this terrace is a genuinely wow moment — near-360 views of the Space Needle, Lake Union, Mount Rainier, and the Cascades. The campsite-chic vibe with old mountaineering gear, cozy couches, and s'mores kits feels fun and un-stuffy for a rooftop bar.
comeHereFor: 360-degree Seattle panorama with s'mores and cocktails
sunDetails: Near-360 views, west side catches afternoon and sunset sun

name: Ivar's Salmon House
description: A Seattle institution with a massive waterfront deck on Lake Union. You're watching seaplanes take off and sailboats cruise by while eating some of the freshest salmon in the city. The patio is huge and unobstructed — one of the best spots to soak up a summer afternoon.
comeHereFor: Waterfront deck with seaplane views
sunDetails: West-facing waterfront deck, afternoon sun until sunset

name: Citizen Collective
description: One of the coolest outdoor spaces in the city — a sprawling astroturf beer garden with fire pits, yard games, a separate outdoor bar, and the Space Needle literally looming over you. Dog-friendly and 21+ in the campfire garden, which gives it a fun, loose neighborhood bar energy.
comeHereFor: Fire pit drinks under the Space Needle with yard games
sunDetails: South/east-facing, morning and midday sun, Space Needle backdrop

name: Bongos
description: Bongos brings full Caribbean energy to Green Lake. The outdoor patio is colorful, open-air, and gets absolutely drenched in sun all day. If you want jerk chicken, rum drinks, and a laid-back island vibe in the middle of Seattle, this is your spot.
comeHereFor: Caribbean vibes and full sun all day
sunDetails: Open-air Caribbean patio, full sun all day
address: 6420 E Green Lake Way N, Seattle, WA 98103

name: Fremont Brewing
description: Fremont Brewing's Urban Beer Garden is exactly what the name promises — a sprawling outdoor space with picnic tables, string lights, and board games tucked into the heart of Fremont. Covered and heated so you can nurse a pint even on a drizzly afternoon. Dog-and-kid-friendly with zero pretension.
comeHereFor: Craft beer in a dog-friendly all-weather beer garden
sunDetails: South/southwest-facing, afternoon sun reaches picnic tables

name: Terra Plata
description: A rooftop herb garden on Capitol Hill with some of the most thoughtful farm-to-table food in the neighborhood. The patio is intimate and green — you're eating surrounded by the ingredients they're cooking with. The cocktails are seasonal and always interesting.
comeHereFor: Rooftop herb garden with farm-to-table food
sunDetails: Rooftop herb garden, afternoon sun with some building shade

name: Frolik Kitchen + Cocktails
description: Frolik's 4,000 sq ft rooftop is one of the largest outdoor spaces in downtown Seattle. Fire pit bar tables, lounge furniture, ping-pong, giant Jenga, and shuffleboard, all with downtown skyline views. Heated and partially tented year-round, and in winter they bring out curling and igloos.
comeHereFor: Year-round rooftop games and cocktails above downtown
sunDetails: Downtown rooftop, gets significant summer sun, surrounded by skyscrapers

name: Old Stove Brewing
description: Old Stove sits right below Pike Place Market with a sprawling deck overlooking Elliott Bay. Great beer, decent bar food, and one of the most prime patio locations in the city. It gets packed on sunny days for good reason.
comeHereFor: Beer on the deck overlooking Elliott Bay
sunDetails: West-facing over Elliott Bay, afternoon sun

name: Duke's Seafood
description: Duke's has been a Seattle staple for years. The South Lake Union location has a big waterfront deck right on Lake Union. Solid seafood, good happy hour, and the kind of reliable patio experience where you know what you're getting — and it's always good.
comeHereFor: Reliable waterfront seafood on Lake Union
sunDetails: Waterfront deck on Lake Union, afternoon sun

name: Situ
description: Situ's courtyard patio in Wallingford is a neighborhood favorite. Great tacos, creative cocktails, and a space that feels casual enough for a Tuesday night but fun enough for a Saturday. The patio catches good afternoon sun and has a relaxed, local energy.
comeHereFor: Tacos and cocktails in a sunny courtyard
sunDetails: Courtyard patio, good afternoon sun

name: Magnuson Cafe and Brewery
description: A proper beer garden tucked inside Magnuson Park. This is the spot for a lazy weekend afternoon — grab a beer, spread out on the open patio, and let the kids run around. The sun exposure is incredible and the park setting makes it feel like a mini-vacation.
comeHereFor: Beer garden vibes in the park with full sun
sunDetails: Open beer garden near the park, full sun until evening
address: 7302 Sand Point Way NE, Seattle, WA 98115

name: Local Public Eatery
description: A big, bustling streetside patio in the heart of SLU. Local Public Eatery nails the casual sports bar vibe with better-than-expected food. The patio is fully covered and heated, so it's a reliable option even on those iffy Seattle days.
comeHereFor: Covered streetside patio that works rain or shine
sunDetails: South-facing patio with good midday sun

name: Monsoon
description: Monsoon's rooftop is a small, intimate perch above Capitol Hill. The Vietnamese food here is some of the best in Seattle — refined and full of flavor. The patio is compact but the combination of excellent food and a unique rooftop setting makes it special.
comeHereFor: Exceptional Vietnamese food on a rooftop
sunDetails: Small rooftop, some afternoon sun depending on season
